newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia money market trade quieter, rates mixed.
newsitem.headline: Croatia money market trade quieter, rates mixed.

text.p: Croatia's money market trade ground to a virtual halt on Thursday due to modest demand and good liquidity in the banking sector, dealers said.
"Banks can manage to square their demand from their own resources so there is little need for interbank borrowings," one dealer said.
She put the morning trade at a meagre 6.5 million kuna, against supply of 111.5 million as banks, savings banks and insurers all offered their surpluses.
The structure also improved in favour of term funds, now accounting for some 20 percent of supply though there was still not enough two-month money, the dealer said.
Rates were mixed. Interbank call money remained lower at 10 percent after Wednesday's cut by 50 basis points, while savings banks still paid 10.5 percent.
One foreign bank creditor charged a higher 15 percent for a one-month loan.
An improved liquidity situation follows a central bank cut in the reserve requirement to 33.85 from 34.85 percent of kuna deposits earlier this month which freed more funds.
Overall banks' balances stood at 492 million kuna on Wednesday with only one bank in the red for 1.8 million kuna, which it squared through the money market.
The banking sector also had 165 million kuna in outstanding Lombard loans, unchanged from last night. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
